(b) M1 for substituting $x = 34$ into both expressions ($2 \times 34$ and $3 \times 34 + 10$); A1 for correct final answers: angle $DAB = 68^\circ$ and angle $BCD = 112^\circ$ (accept if angles sum to check to 180).

questions.correct_answer: Angle OBC = Angle OCB = 26 degrees (shown using alternate segment theorem: angle BCA = 64 degrees, then angle BOC = 128 degrees by angle at centre = twice angle at circumference, then base angles of isosceles triangle OBC = (180-128)/2 = 26 degrees)

M1 for identifying angle BCA = 64 degrees using the alternate segment theorem (angle between tangent TAS and chord AB equals angle in alternate segment, angle ACB)
A1 for correctly stating angle BOC = 2 x 64 = 128 degrees using the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference (both angles subtended by arc AB... reasoning must correctly link angle ACB at circumference to angle BOC at centre, both standing on arc AB)
M1 for stating triangle OBC is isosceles because OB = OC (radii of the same circle)
M1 for using angle sum of triangle OBC = 180 degrees: angle OBC + angle OCB + angle BOC = 180
A1 (dependent on all previous marks) for correct conclusion: since triangle OBC is isosceles, angle OBC = angle OCB = (180 - 128)/2 = 26 degrees, fully justified with each theorem named (alternate segment theorem, angle at centre theorem, isosceles triangle base angles)
